title: Chamfers or Radius and Relief Grooves on Toothing and Involute Splined
topics: Grinding wheel clearance on internal splines
Exit chamfer specifications for splined features
rules: When fitting coupling slide-guide is not possible, a chamfer with grinding wheel angle must be made on tooth edge (see picture D015DA)
For internal involute splines: chamfer at 15° must be made in all cases except for splined toothing inside flange discs (e.g., flanged hub or brake's housing)
Radius R on toothing must be made where necessary for fitting axe or centring in next machining processes
Exit chamfer must have an angle value different to 30° to respect condition of fitting with engraved angle
dimensions: Chamfer angle: 15° for internal involute splines
Exit chamfer: angle different from 30° required
Dimension 0.5 shown on drawing D015C (chamfer depth)
Dimension 9÷12 shown on drawing D015E (relief groove width)
manufacturing_notes: Grinding wheel clearance must be considered when designing internal splines
Relief grooves must provide clearance for fitting axe or centering operations
Exit chamfer angle must differ from 30° to enable fitting with engraved angle
For internal splines in flange discs, radius R is used instead of chamfer
training_guidance: When modeling involute splines (internal), always include 15° chamfer at tooth edges unless component is a flange disc
For flange disc applications (flanged hub or brake housing), use radius R instead of chamfer
Exit chamfers on splined features must not be 30° - choose different angle to accommodate engraved angle mating
Include relief grooves with adequate width (9-12mm reference) for subsequent machining operations
When designing toothing that cannot accommodate slide-guide coupling, add chamfer matching grinding wheel angle at tooth edge
summary: This standard defines chamfer and relief groove requirements for toothed and involute splined components. Internal involute splines require 15° chamfers except in flange disc applications where radius is used. Exit chamfers must use angles other than 30° to enable proper fitting with engraved angles, and relief grooves must provide clearance for subsequent machining operations.
